title: Granular lane cost & SLA cutover PRD + deployment checklist for hosted inference endpoints
creator: Ava Chen
description: Summary: This PRD defines the product requirements, acceptance criteria, and launch checklist for introducing granular lane pricing and SLA profiles across the hosted inference endpoints (chat/completions/embeddings/rerank). The goal is to expose cost-tiered lanes that let customers trade off latency and price while allowing Redwood to perform zero-downtime cutovers and graded degradations between lanes when capacity or incidents occur. The feature surface includes: lane definition and metadata, per-lane SLA and cost band configuration, API surface to request or opt into lanes, backend routing rules and fallback policy, telemetry and billing hooks, canary and cutover playbook, and migration guidance for existing customers.
background_and_goals: Background: Customers ask for more predictable unit economics and the ability to choose latencies vs. price when calling hosted endpoints. Internally we need a mechanism to group capacity into lanes with explicit cost profiles (e.g., premium-low-latency, standard-balanced, economy-high-throughput) and a safe way to perform capacity cutovers without dropping in-flight requests. Goals: 1) Provide explicit lane options surfaced via API/Console and SDKs. 2) Map each lane to measurable SLAs (p50/p95 latency, error rate, availability) and cost multipliers. 3) Guarantee zero-downtime cutovers between lane mappings for a tenant (transparent fallback). 4) Make rollouts auditable and reversible with telemetry gates. 5) Minimize changes required by customers — default behavior remains backward compatible.
scope_inclusions: - API: request_lanes (optional) query parameter and lane preference header; console UI to view lane costs and expected SLOs; SDK flag. - Server-side: lane metadata registry, routing policy engine, versioned mapping store per-tenant, preflight health checks, graceful KV/prefix cache preservation across cutovers. - Observability: lane-level telemetry, cost attribution tagging, rollout traces, SLA breach alerts. - Launch artifacts: canary and cutover runbook, customer migration doc, billing mapping update, e2e test suite.
scope_exclusions: - Billing pricebook UI changes (handled by billing team separately) - Dedicated/Private deployment automation (out of scope for initial launch) - New model flavors or quantization suggestions (handled by Optimize later)
requirements: 1) API/SDK: optional lane selector (string) and lane-fallback-policy (enum: prefer, strict, degrade). 2) Console: lane catalog page showing p50/p95 historical and projected cost-per-1k-tokens. 3) Routing: deterministic per-tenant lane mapping with atomic swap support and automatic fallback to compatible lane if capacity insufficient. 4) Safety: preflight canary with synthetic traffic validation and automatic rollback if telemetry gates fail. 5) Telemetry: tags on every request for lane_id, routing_decision, fallback_reason, and billing_tag. 6) Acceptance: performance targets for each lane are validated against traffic mix and load tests. 7) Migration helpers: bulk-assignment tool for enterprise tenants and opt-in CLI for self-serve customers.
tradeoffs_and_anti_requirements: Tradeoffs: Introducing lanes increases control plane complexity and risk of misrouting; we prioritize readability of lane semantics over maximal flexibility. We will avoid exposing low-level placement controls to customers in v1 to reduce complexity. Anti-requirements: Do not require customers to re-author prompts or rework prompt engineering for lane adoption. No changes to response semantics or random seed/determinism guarantees except where explicit lane-based quality regressions are documented.
acceptance_criteria: API: lane selector accepted by chat/completions/embeddings/rerank endpoints with valid enums documented.
Console: lane catalog page available with historical p50/p95 and sample cost projection for top 5 models.
Routing: atomic per-tenant lane mapping swap completes with zero dropped requests in synthetic cutover tests under normal load.
Perf: premium lane p95 latency within 10% of baseline SLA target for the same model; economy lane achieves >=25% lower cost per token on average in load tests.
Reliability: no more than 0.1% increased error rate during cutover window in staged canary runs.
Rollback: automated rollback triggers on two telemetry gates (latency spike >30% p95 or error rate >0.5%) during canary and cutover runs.
Billing: every request contains billing_tag and maps to cost band in logs; sample billing export shows correct lane attribution for 7-day window.
Docs: migration guide, API docs, and console help articles published and linked from release notes.
Sign-offs: PM, ENG (runtime + routing), SRE, Billing, and Legal have approved launch checklist items.
Security: security_review_required false but standard telemetry PII review completed; no customer payloads persisted beyond existing retention policies.
launch_checklist: Code merge: routing engine changes merged and green (ENG-84221).
API docs: lane selector fields documented and published in SDK changelog.
Console: lane catalog U/X built and smoke-tested in staging; pricing UI placeholders linked to billing team.
Telemetry: lane tags emitted; dashboards created for lane p50/p95, error rate, and fallback counts.
Canary plan: reserve 5% traffic slice for internal Canary tenants and synthetic traffic during initial rollouts.
Load test: synthetic spike test at 150% normal load with cutover validated and no dropped requests.
Billing mapping: billing export pipeline validated for lane attribution for 7 days in staging.
Runbooks: cutover and rollback runbooks reviewed and dry-run executed by SRE on staging cluster.
Customer comms: email template and in-console banner drafted for enterprise customers outlining lane benefits and migration options.
Compliance: telemetry/data retention check completed; Legal acknowledgement added to release notes.
Launch window: set initial cutover maintenance window with on-call ENG + SRE overlap for 2 hours post-cutover.
Post-launch: 72-hour monitoring window with prioritized alerting and daily postmortem checklist ready.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (internal): Feature flags enabled for internal and dev tenants. Phase 1 (canary): 5% internal traffic plus synthetic validation. Phase 2 (enterprise opt-in): invite enterprise customers to opt into lanes with support assistance and bulk-assignment tooling. Phase 3 (general availability): open lane selector to self-serve with default behavior preserved for existing callers. Cutover approach: per-tenant atomic mapping swap via config store; in-flight requests routed to old lane until completion; new requests use new mapping. Fallback behavior: automatic fallback to nearest-compatible lane if preferred lane is capacity constrained; fallback_reason annotated for telemetry and billing.
test_plan: Unit tests for lane selector parsing and header handling; integration tests for routing engine path selection; golden tests for billing tag mapping; e2e staging test: synthetic workload reproducing production percentile distributions across models for chat/completions/embeddings/rerank. Performance tests: p50/p95 measurement under 1x and 1.5x load for each lane. Cutover test: simultaneous atomic swap while generating 10k in-flight requests verifying none are dropped and latency curves remain within acceptance thresholds.
telemetry_metrics: cutover_duration_seconds - time from start of mapping swap to last in-flight request completion
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Misrouted requests during atomic swaps. Mitigation: perform atomic swap via transactional config store and validate with synthetic checks before unflagging. Risk: Unexpected SLA regressions for economy lane on certain models. Mitigation: conservative cost targets during initial launch and model-level exclusions for lanes until validated. Risk: Billing discrepancies. Mitigation: parallel billing export validation in staging for 7 days and reconciliation scripts.
decisions: Expose lane selector as optional parameter rather than required field to preserve backward compatibility.
Do not support custom per-tenant lane creation in v1; lanes are centrally defined and versioned by product.
Fallback policy semantics: default to 'prefer' which attempts preferred lane then falls back when capacity constrained.
Cutover style: atomic config swap per-tenant with in-flight graceful draining rather than live-migration of in-flight requests.
open_questions: Should we surface historical lane cost trends in Console for more than 30 days? (ops/storage tradeoff).
Is there appetite from billing to accept lane-level discounts in month-1 or should we postpone discounts to month-2?
Do we default new customers to economy lane or balanced lane?
Should SDKs expose a prioritized list of acceptable lanes instead of a single selector?
